inserted_rule.title: Establish the ECL model before alleging a staging defect
inserted_rule.rule_text: Classify the instrument and establish whether simplified lifetime ECL is mandatory or elected. For IFRS15 trade receivables without a significant financing component, use the required lifetime approach; for eligible receivables with a significant financing component, verify the entity's policy choice. Where simplified lifetime ECL applies, do not demand general-model Stage1/2 migrations or a 30-DPD SICR backstop. Evaluate provision-matrix losses using historical/current/forward-looking evidence. Zero ELRs alone prove neither adequacy nor manipulation. If policy applicability is uncertain, record the precise uncertainty rather than invent a staging breach. Required evidence: Instrument/transaction type, terms/financing component, policy where choice exists, aging/matrix and loss experience/forward adjustments; physical-page citations. Exceptions: General-model instruments, POCI and other eligible policy choices must be assessed under their own requirements; do not relabel purchased portfolios as trade-service receivables. Avoid double counting: Do not add an arbitrary credit haircut on top of an already modeled expected cash loss or add loss allowances twice. Fail example: “0% at31 days proves failure to transfer to Stage2” where simplified lifetime ECL is established. Pass example: “Lifetime ECL policy established; no SICR-stage test; zero matrix rates require portfolio-specific support, not automatic acceptance.”

limits: Registry/prompt wiring verified; future model compliance is not demonstrated. Section prompt integration unchanged.
